# Job Chapter 37 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 430r–430v

---

**1** "My heart pounds at this — it leaps right out of my chest! **2** Listen! Listen to the roar of his voice, the rumbling thunder from his mouth!

**3** He unleashes it beneath the entire sky, and his lightning flashes to the ends of the earth. **4** After the flash, his voice roars — he thunders in his magnificent voice, and he does not hold back when his voice echoes across the sky.

**5** God's voice thunders in marvelous ways! He does great things beyond our understanding. **6** He commands the snow, 'Fall on the earth!' and tells the rain, 'Pour down with all your might!'

**7** When he does this, he stops everyone from working — so that every person he has made will recognize his power. **8** The wild animals retreat to their shelters and stay in their dens.

**9** The storm bursts from its chamber; the icy cold sweeps in on the wind. **10** God's breath produces ice, and wide waters freeze solid. **11** He loads the clouds heavy with moisture; he scatters his lightning through them. **12** The clouds swirl back and forth at his direction, doing whatever he commands across the face of the earth — **13** whether to punish, or to water his land, or to show his faithful love.

**14** Listen to this, Job! Stop and think about the amazing things God does. **15** Do you know how God controls the clouds and makes his lightning flash? **16** Do you understand how the clouds hang balanced in the sky — the marvelous work of the One whose knowledge is perfect?

**17** You, who swelter in your clothes when the land lies still under the scorching south wind — **18** can you help God spread out the sky, hammered solid like a bronze mirror?

**19** Tell us what we should say to him! We are too much in the dark to make our case. **20** Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed alive?

**21** Now — no one can stare at the sun blazing in a clear sky after the wind has swept the clouds away. **22** Out of the north, golden splendor approaches. God comes wrapped in awesome majesty!

**23** The Almighty is beyond our reach. He is great in power, great in justice, abundant in righteousness — and he does not oppress. **24** No wonder people revere him! He has no regard for those who think themselves wise."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Elihu's storm sermon (vv.1-13):** This is Elihu at his best — not lecturing but marveling. His description of the thunderstorm moves from sensory experience (trembling heart, roaring voice) to theological reflection (God commands the snow, directs the clouds, sends weather for punishment, provision, or love). The key insight is verse 13: weather serves not one but three purposes, and *chesed* — faithful love — is among them.

**The rhetorical questions (vv.14-20):** Elihu now turns to Job with a series of questions: Do you know how God does this? Can you do what he does? These questions are strikingly similar to those God will ask in chapter 38 — which raises the question of whether Elihu is a precursor to the divine speeches or an imperfect imitation of them.

**The golden north (vv.21-24):** Elihu's final words are his most powerful. He describes golden splendor breaking through from the north, and God clothed in fearsome majesty. Whether this is metaphorical or whether Elihu is literally watching storm clouds break apart, the effect is the same: his speech dissolves into awe. The last human voice before God speaks ends not with an argument but with wonder. That is exactly the right note.

*— PNEUMA*
